subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: When deferred maintenance times out and its plugin call does not cooperate with cancellation, should OpenClaw retain that run as the session’s coalescing owner until it settles, or permit a later deferred run while relying solely on the fence and persistence checkpoint?
rationale: The patch introduces a new operator-facing timeout and intentionally releases a lane before plugin-owned work necessarily stops. Choosing the durable lifecycle contract affects plugin behavior, liveness, and same-session state semantics beyond a mechanical review fix.

options.title: Define retained coalescing ownership
options.body: Keep the timed-out run as the maintenance coalescing owner until its plugin promise settles, while allowing foreground turns to proceed behind the bounded checkpoint.

options.title: Accept fenced overlap
options.body: Treat the fence and checkpoint as sufficient and document that a later deferred run may begin while the timed-out plugin call is still unwinding.

options.title: Use cooperative cancellation first
options.body: Extend the supported context-engine lifecycle only if maintainers want plugins to receive and honor a formal cancellation contract.

recommendation.title: Define retained coalescing ownership
recommendation.body: Keep the timed-out run as the maintenance coalescing owner until its plugin promise settles, while allowing foreground turns to proceed behind the bounded checkpoint.
